text:
anya: quick question about flag resolution order — hit an edge case in the rollout tests.
anya: config: org:true, project:null, route:false, model:true. Which one actually wins if the route is active? also what if the route gets deleted but the model remains?
sam: route-level should win when the route exists, even if model=true. route is the most specific path-based override.
jordan: agreed on route-first. but watch out for how we define 'route exists' — unpublished vs deleted vs renamed matters.
luis: canary audience merging question: if org enables a feature for 100% but route disables for the canary segment, does the route block for that segment only? or fully?
sam: route flags are applied at request-time after audience check. so route=false will block for all audiences on that route. if you want partial block, set route.canary or model.canary.
anya: here's the snippet I was looking at from resolver tests:
```
// simplified precedence we thought was: route -> model -> project -> org\// but failing when route is removed during rollout
resolveFlag(request) {
  if (routeFlag !== undefined) return routeFlag;
  if (modelFlag !== undefined) return modelFlag;
  if (projectFlag !== undefined) return projectFlag;
  return orgFlag;
}
```
anya: problem: if route is deleted mid-rollout, requests still get matched to model handler and we expect modelFlag to apply. current resolver sometimes returns org default because route metadata was stale.
jordan: that's a bug — resolver should treat a missing route as "no route flag" (fallthrough to model). we need to guard against stale route cache.
luis: +1. Also need to be careful about audience logic order: we evaluate audience -> route match -> flag resolution, or route match -> flag resolution -> audience? we should be explicit.
sam: proposal: evaluation order: 1) resolve which object the request maps to (route and model IDs). 2) evaluate audiences (canary segmenting) scoped to the resolved object. 3) resolve flags by specificity: route -> model -> project -> org. That way route presence is canonical.
anya: that sounds right. Can we add a defensive check: if route ID maps to a deleted route, treat as no route. And add unit test where route TTL drops between requests.
ci-bot: deploy-hook: new test added to branch flag-resolver/fallthrough — CI queued.
jordan: action items: (1) Sam to PR resolver change to explicitly check route existence, (2) Anya to add regression tests for deleted route fallthrough, (3) Luis to add a doc note on audience evaluation order.
sam: I'll open the PR today.
anya: thanks — filing follow-ups in the ticket: https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/INFR-4125
luis: small note on UX: Console should show when a route-level flag is orphaned (route deleted) and show fallback value from model/project/org to avoid confusion.
jordan: agreed, add console flag badge: "fallthrough".
anya: ok — tagging @sam @luis @jordan for visibility. :thumbsup:
